newsitem.title: USA: FBI lures thieves to New Jersey in huge goods sting.
newsitem.headline: FBI lures thieves to New Jersey in huge goods sting.

text.p: An undercover FBI operation lured suspected thieves to a New Jersey warehouse where they stored $38 million worth of stolen goods from string bikinis to pet supplies, officials said Tuesday.

In the biggest stolen-property sting in FBI history, according to U.S. Attorney for New Jersey Faith Hochberg, indictments were brought against more than 60 people in 12 states and she said 30 more suspects were being sought.

Hochberg told a news conference that the operation out of a Bergen County warehouse began 19 months ago, targeting men and women believed to have embezzled or stolen goods while they were being legally traded between states.

Federal agents established a cover company called Norlock to receive the stolen items, which included oranges, string bikinis, exercise equipment, beer, seafood, cosmetics, cookware, margarine, beach toys, pet supplies, towels, mens and womens clothing, office furniture and sewing machines.
Arrest warrants were issued Tuesday in New Jersey, Ohio, Florida, Georgia, Maine, Maryland, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, Vermont and Wisconsin, said special agent Barry Mawn.
A temporary courthouse was set up at Newark International Airport to handle paperwork. All defendants will be released on bail and arraigned at a later date, officials said.

If convicted of embezzling or receiving and possessing stolen property, the maximum penalty is 10 years in federal prison and a fine of from $250,000 up to twice the amount of loss or gain from the crime.
